record.paper_title: Some Open Questions in Quiver Gauge Theory
record.context_brief: Relations among tau_G, tau_R, and tau_B
record.original_question: Three modular parameters appear in this setting: tau_G from the geometry of the torus in the Gorenstein singularity, tau_R from the isoradial brane tiling, and tau_B from the Belyi pair. What is the precise relationship among tau_G, tau_R, and tau_B?

evidence.quote: Question 26. What is the precise relation between τG, τR and τB?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $X$ be a toric Calabi–Yau threefold realized as an affine Gorenstein singularity, with associated 4d $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal quiver gauge theory encoded by a brane tiling, i.e. a bipartite graph $\Gamma$ drawn on a real two-torus $T^2$. Three complex-structure (modular) parameters in the upper half-plane $\mathbb{H}$ are naturally attached to this data:

(1) $\tau_G$, the geometric modular parameter. It is the complex structure of the two-torus appearing in the mirror geometry / Sasaki–Einstein description of the Gorenstein singularity $X$, equivalently the complex structure on the torus fibre extracted from the volume/$a$-maximization data of $X$.

(2) $\tau_R$, the isoradial (R-charge) modular parameter. Performing $a$-maximization fixes the superconformal $R$-charges of the bifundamental fields; the bipartite graph $\Gamma$ then admits an isoradial embedding in which the rhombus angle of each edge equals $\pi$ times the corresponding $R$-charge. The fundamental domain of this isoradial embedding is a parallelogram in $\mathbb{C}$ whose modular parameter is $\tau_R\in\mathbb{H}$.

(3) $\tau_B$, the Belyi modular parameter. The brane tiling $\Gamma$ corresponds to a torus Belyi pair: an elliptic curve $E_B=\mathbb{C}/(\mathbb{Z}+\tau_B\mathbb{Z})$ together with a holomorphic map $\beta:E_B\to\mathbb{P}^1$ ramified only over $\{0,1,\infty\}$, whose dessin d'enfant on $E_B$ reproduces $\Gamma$. The complex structure of the source elliptic curve defines $\tau_B\in\mathbb{H}$.

Problem. Determine the precise relationship among the three modular parameters $\tau_G$, $\tau_R$, and $\tau_B$ associated to an arbitrary toric Calabi–Yau Gorenstein singularity and its brane tiling. Specifically, find an explicit (e.g. modular, algebraic, or analytic) map, valid for every such tiling, expressing $\tau_G$, $\tau_R$, and $\tau_B$ in terms of one another (or characterize precisely when they coincide modulo $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$).
artifact.status_search_result: The three complex structures τ_G, τ_R, τ_B associated to brane tilings are known to be generically inequivalent; partial work (e.g. on a "modular Mahler flow" and on isoradial/Belyi comparisons in specific examples such as the conifold and Y^{p,q} families) gives equalities of j-invariants in special cases, but no general formula relating all three is established. The question is listed as an open problem in the literature on quiver gauge theory.

status_evidence.title: Gauge Theories and Dessins d'Enfants: Beyond the Torus
status_evidence.snippet: Different τ_R values for various phases can share the same j-function value and are thus modular equivalent; comparisons among Belyi, isoradial and geometric complex structures are discussed.
status_evidence.claim: The three modular parameters are studied and compared case by case but no general relation is known.

status_evidence.title: The beta ansatz: a tale of two complex structures
status_evidence.snippet: a-maximization in the context of isoradial embeddings of the dimer associates a complex structure to the torus, determined by the R-charges, which can be compared with the Belyi complex structure.
status_evidence.claim: The relationship between τ_R and τ_B is investigated but only partially understood.
